notes: What a written procedure is worth when nothing has ever been tried. Documentation is how an experienced practitioner starts on a case they have never seen: it is a real basis for a proposal and it is not experience. This policy keeps those two things apart.

eligibility.notes: A document must actually be about this component and this symptom. Lexical relevance is enough to surface a document for a human to read; it is not enough to propose a cause from it.

freshness.notes: A procedure validated last month and one validated eighteen months ago are not equally reliable descriptions of a system that has changed since. Credit decays linearly between the two bounds rather than expiring on a date, because nothing about a document changes on its anniversary.

ceiling.notes: A documented hypothesis can never reach the accelerated plan and can never clear the approval requirement, however trusted and current the document is. Trust in a document is trust in its author; it is not evidence that the remedy works on this system. The ceiling sits below the MEDIUM confidence band deliberately, so a documented proposal cannot be mistaken for a validated one at a glance.

disclosure.notes: The recommendation must say which document it came from and that nothing comparable has been resolved before. A proposal a human cannot trace is a proposal a human cannot validate, and validation is the entire purpose of making it.

refutation.notes: A human rejecting a proposed cause is evidence that it did not hold here, and it is weighed as evidence. It is not a ban. A human can reject correctly and a human can reject wrongly, and a system that treats one rejection as final has made that person's error unfalsifiable. Support therefore decays with each rejection but never reaches zero: if nothing better accounts for the presentation, the account is offered again, ranked lower, with the prior rejection and the name of the person who made it disclosed so the next reviewer can weigh it themselves.

reconsultation.notes: A recalled pattern used to end the search. That is right when the pattern is strong and wrong when it is not: a thinly evidenced pattern is exactly the case where the written record is most likely to know something the system does not. Below this threshold the documentation reasoner runs anyway and its proposals are carried as alternatives, so the weak recall is put beside the current procedure rather than in place of it.
reconsultation.recency_notes: Knowledge is not static. A post-incident review written after the first occurrence, or a runbook revised since, is precisely the material that should change the second response — and a system that consults documentation only when it remembers nothing would never see it. Documentation validated more recently than the pattern's last recorded case is surfaced explicitly.
